transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. We need to finalize the launch plan for the new usage-based billing meter. As you know, it's passed sandbox integration tests and we're targeting next month's billing cycle. The current draft proposes an immediate broad launch, two-decimal half-up rounding, 90 days of raw usage-event retention, and no mandatory invoice-preview review. Before I approve anything, I want to hear from each of you — billing engineering, finance operations, privacy, and customer support. Let's start with billing engineering: any concerns with the integration or the proposed configuration?

transcript.text: I have a concern I need to raise. During a separate billing reconciliation task, I validated an older contract adapter and confirmed that our annual-credit contracts require six-decimal meter precision and half-even rounding to avoid cumulative invoice discrepancies. The current draft's proposed two-decimal half-up rounding would be incompatible with those contracts. This finding hasn't been added to the launch checklist yet, and I think it needs to be addressed before we proceed.

transcript.text: I need to share a finance operations requirement. I confirmed with revenue accounting this morning that the first launch requires invoice previews for exactly 50 accounts and a maximum measured variance of 10 basis points before production billing can be approved. This directly conflicts with the current draft's proposal of no mandatory invoice-preview review.
